transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-19 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom / Fireflies transcript
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Jorge Martinez (Redwood CSM); Mark Rivera (AtlasPay - Head of ML); Sofia Patel (AtlasPay - Platform Eng); Evan Liu (AtlasPay - Product); Tara Singh (AtlasPay - SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on POC throughput results; discuss continuous batching and concurrency tradeoffs; action items to run larger batch sims and share configs + traffic histogram. Some transcription errors expected.
Topics: throughput, continuous batching, concurrency targets, queueing/latency SLOs, KV cache behavior, fallback model routing, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, goal for today is quick status and decide on next perf runs.
[00:08] Mark: yep, thanks Alex, we did the 4-concurrency run last week, saw about 28% cost reduction but p95 bumped a bit, so we wanna see how continuous batching at higher concurrency behaves.
[00:22] Priya: cool, quick context: our continuous batching engine tries to pack small requests up to a batch size, there's a tradeoff between batching window and tail latency. we recommended two knobs: target concurrency and max batching window.
[00:36] Sofia: just to confirm, our SLO is p95 < 350ms for interactive flows, bursty payments background can be higher.
[00:42] Alex: got it. today we'll review the logs Priya shared, call out hotspots, then agree on next bench.
[00:49] [crosstalk]
[00:52] Evan: quick question, when you say concurrency 8, is that per model instance or per pool?
[00:56] Priya: per worker process, so if you have 4 workers on a node, effective concurrency is 4 * 8 concurrently inflight. but smart routing can cap inflight to match the pool target.
[01:10] Tara: and queueing, does RW runtime do queueing or we have to manage an external queue?
[01:14] Priya: Redwood runtime supports internal queueing with backpressure; we also support a fronting queue for longer waits. for the POC we used internal queue with short max-wait 50ms.
[01:28] Mark: the run we did had 100ms batching window, seemed to help throughput but some p95 spikes. transcript note: sometimes "p95 spikes" transcribed as "p 95 spikes" in docs.
[01:36] Priya: right, with 100ms window we pack more tokens but a few requests wait and that pushes tails. that's where target concurrency helps---you can increase worker concurrency so each request is sampled into earlier batches.
[01:50] Alex: can you walk through numbers from last week's run? I have the spreadsheet but maybe call out the key lines.
[01:56] Priya: sure, high level: baseline hosted run (1x concurrency, no cont-batching) avg throughput 420 rps, 4-concurrency continuous-batch gave 2.7x throughput ~1140 rps, p95 went from 280ms to 420ms in one path. cost per token dropped by ~28%.
[02:18] Sofia: and latency-sensitive paths were the chat UI, those we need p95 < 350ms, payments backend okay at p95 < 800ms.
[02:26] Mark: asked earlier about kv cache—are we seeing cache hits improve with continuous batching?
[02:30] Priya: good point. KV cache hit-rate is orthogonal but helps decode time. packing doesn't change cache hit-rate much unless you're grouping requests with similar prefixes; we saw slight improvement for repeated session traffic. note: sometimes "KV cache" comes through as "K V cache" in the transcript.
[02:50] Jorge (CSM): small note, customer asked for a config template so their infra team can replicate.
[02:54] Priya: yes we'll share that. recommended starting point: concurrency target = 8, max_batch_window = 50ms, worker_count = 4 per GPU, queueing_policy = drop-oldest (for interactive), fallback_model = small-quantized for overloaded cases.
[03:10] Evan: drop-oldest meaning requests will be rejected or kicked? we can't drop payment requests.
[03:15] Priya: good call — for payment-critical routes use queueing_policy = hold + alert and route heavy or non-interactive flows to dedicated lower-priority pool. for interactive UI use drop-oldest to preserve p95.
[03:30] Sofia: can Redwood runtime route by tag? we tag calls with route=payments vs route=ui?
[03:34] Alex: yep, you can route by header or route name; we can set different policies per route.
[03:40] Tara: latency SLOs—we also need to test tail under 30s bursts, last time a backend spike crushed concurrency.
[03:46] Priya: next bench should include a 30s burst at 3x baseline to see queueing; we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second.
[03:56] Mark: what about quantization? we saw quality drop on some prompts with int8. any recommendation?
[04:02] Priya: for now use q4_0 or q4_1 for decoder-only; int8 can be good but watch regressions. we can run A/B on quality metrics using your eval set.
[04:14] [pause]
[04:18] Sofia: Priya, in the logs you sent there's a weird spike at 13:12, is that from a single tenant?
[04:22] Priya: I think that was a concurrency build-up while a model load happened; the runtime did a cold load fallback to host-model which spiked CPU. recommendation: warm model instances during deploys or use pinning to avoid cold starts.
[04:36] Mark: deploy pinning, right. can Redwood do model pinning per pool?
[04:40] Alex: yes, you can pin model versions to dedicated pools; that avoids cold start and gives predictable mem usage.
[04:46] Evan: we need an estimate of cost at target throughput—can you give a rough blowout?
[04:50] Alex: rough calc: at 8 concurrency with continuous batching and 4 workers per node on a standard NVIDIA A10k equi, you'd get roughly 2.8k rps per GPU at this model family, cost delta about 1.8x vs baseline hosted; we'll send the detailed sheet.
[05:06] Sofia: that 2.8k rps assumes good batching and prefix locality right?
[05:10] Priya: correct; if your traffic is highly diverse batching helps less. we'll simulate both uniform and real histogram.
[05:18] Tara: on security, when we move to dedicated or private, what about KMS and audit logs?
[05:22] Alex: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log retention; we can include SOC2 artifacts—we'll route security questions to our security engs.
[05:30] [inaudible] Speaker 1: sorry can you repeat the concurrency number?
[05:33] Priya: recommended target concurrency to test = 8, and also try 12 for comparison.
[05:38] Mark: can we see end-to-end p99 for the 12 run or that will be too bad?
[05:42] Priya: p99 will likely be worse with naive settings, that's why we tune batch window. a shorter max-window helps p99 but reduces throughput. it's a multi-objective tuning.
[05:54] Evan: operationally, what's easiest for us to run? we have a k8s deployment with a small pool, do you provide helm charts or manifest?
[06:00] Alex: yes helm chart and manifests; Priya will share a sample values.yaml with recommended worker_count and concurrency.
[06:06] Priya: also we'll include a small bench script we used for repeatable runs. link in notes: (see shared drive)
[06:12] Mark: timeline—after the new benchmarks we want a final review the week of Nov 24. is that feasible?
[06:18] Alex: yes priya can run the bench and we can reconvene Nov 26 for final.
[06:22] Priya: I'll run two bench suites: 8-concurrency baseline and 12-concurrency test, each with burst sim and steady-state 15m run.
[06:32] Sofia: please also include the queue depth histogram per worker so we can see build up.
[06:36] Priya: will do.
[06:38] Jorge: I'll follow up with the deck and the pricing sheet.
[06:42] Mark: anything else on risk or blockers? security review is only blocker if they need on-prem before pilot scales.
[06:50] Alex: ok last bit, next steps recap — run benches, share config + logs, customer to share traffic histogram, schedule Nov 26 final sync.
[06:58] Evan: thanks all.
[07:00] [meeting end]
